Messages.Author: henrik isaksson
Messages.Body:
So, which cards do you love/hate so far?

Ma favourites:
Carver's Meat Packing and Storage - great for weenie-bashing

Elysium: Sforzesco Castle - saves a qouple of wakes for walls

Recalled to the founder - can mess up some decks really bad!

Fall of the Camarilla/Sabbat - huge effect/high oppurtunity cost

Dragonbound - goodies for combat decks are always nice

Mylan Horseed (Goblin) - Will go in very many of my decks. Fatties without
fortitude need all the help they can get!

Perfectionist - probably the only of the new archetypes I'll play with.

Sleep of Reason - Lot's of new cards make it harder for vampires to keep
their blood, making them targets for this. Try with Hazamiel, Free states
rant and a few freak drives!

The Unmasking - will be great in any ally deck. Shambling horde, weenie
brujah allies, war ghouls. For total madness, combine with Absimiliards
army. (we had that combo in play yesterday, noone could do anything)

Starvation of Marena - good solid card

(Mc) Flurry Of Action
Also more actions for none-fortitude... great!

The Erciyes Fragments - not gehenna but almost... This card is super!
Perfect for taking usefull stuff like blood dolls or wakes.

The bad ones:

Jacob, The Glitch - this vampire would be great if only I could find a way
of forcing him on my prey... =) Will only play if I really want to empty my
library for some reason...

Conniver - really should be trifle... Only way I'm seeing that it could be
used is if grand prey is a voter, but how can you assure that? Will never
play this!

Sleep Unseen - Cost one blood, after a succesfull action making you almost
immune to rush for one round? That crap!

Muhandis - This guy is seriously underpowered compared to some other guys.
He didn't need that drawback.

Thought?

/henrik isaksson

Messages.Author: Aramis
Messages.Body:
"henrik isaksson" <PLEASEDONTSP...@spray.se> wrote in message news:<2hc62eF...@uni-berlin.de>...

> So, which cards do you love/hate so far?

Yeah, but probably at it's most effective in weenie-creating decks.
If your weenies get knocked down, make them hostages to feed your
bigger guys. I'm thinking it's a nice blood gain engine for
Embrace/3rd/Creation Rites decks.

I was sad to see this card printed. I like my clan-based decks!

I'll see decks dedicated to getting these in play. That said, I'm

push. Fattie vote is particularly defended by packing a few Emergency
Preparations and just killing the Fall when they see it coming.

> Dragonbound - goodies for combat decks are always nice

Probably my favorite card in the set.

> Mylan Horseed (Goblin) - Will go in very many of my decks. Fatties without
> fortitude need all the help they can get!

I expect Mylan to the most contested ally yet. Pack the Entrancements
and Far Mastery...

the same bounce too.

> Sleep of Reason - Lot's of new cards make it harder for vampires to keep

> rant and a few freak drives!

Yeah, I was also sad to see this one. DEM didn't really need more

> brujah allies, war ghouls. For total madness, combine with Absimiliards
> army. (we had that combo in play yesterday, noone could do anything)

I don't know about this one. Ally block decks? Ally decks still seem
pretty weak to me.

> (Mc) Flurry Of Action
> Also more actions for none-fortitude... great!

Yeah, I was hoping for a CEL-based Freak Drive, but this is close
enough for me.

> The Erciyes Fragments - not gehenna but almost... This card is super!
> Perfect for taking usefull stuff like blood dolls or wakes.

Another of the cards I expect to see heavily contested in the coming
months. The card is almost too good...

> The bad ones:
>
> Jacob, The Glitch - this vampire would be great if only I could find a way
> of forcing him on my prey... =) Will only play if I really want to empty my
> library for some reason...

I agree. His flaw is just too much IMO.

> Conniver - really should be trifle... Only way I'm seeing that it could be
> used is if grand prey is a voter, but how can you assure that? Will never
> play this!

Um... no. This card screams "BOUNCE". That all of your Connivers can
cash in on the same action is also really good.

> Sleep Unseen - Cost one blood, after a succesfull action making you almost
> immune to rush for one round? That crap!

This is a really strong defense though, "no D actions" beats much more
than simply rush decks. I think OBF/DEM will use this card the most
because they didn't really have a means of combat defense before.
Also note that the card is freely cyclable on your actions as opposed
to Majesty/Obedience which could clog your hand if you don't get into
combat.

My additional good/bad list...

Good: Alastor, Leadership Vacuum, Reformation.
Bad: Kaymakli Nightmares, simply because it gives even more firepower
to the Anarch Revolt/Computer Hacking decks.

> /henrik isaksson

Aramis

*still waiting to play with his Gehenna toys...*

Messages.Author: ThunderFoot
Messages.Body:
niko...@hotmail.com (Nikolaj Wendt) wrote in message news:<22f564b8.04052...@posting.google.com>...

> So the opposing minion can burn a blood to prevent all damage from
> your nice little flying cycle....

We had a lovely traffic accident the other day, someone running away
in their limo (with Jackie Therman) only to crash into a cycle.

The damage prevention is really the crucial part of the card, it
happens regardless of whether they cancel the damage to themselves. If
someone has a Magnum and you play this at inferior then you only take
one damage and they take either one or three. If you had a Sewer lid
then you'd take 2 and they'd take 3 for sure.
With a weenie (Or any kind of combat really) deck there are definitely
times when blood will be tight and you'd rather take one less damage
regardless of how much damage the other person is going to take.

ThunderFoot.

Messages.Author: kushiel
Messages.Body:
"Wes" <gh...@NYETSPAMmnsi.net> wrote in message news:<c8re6...@enews4.newsguy.com>...


Conniver isn't good? What about weenie Auspex? (I also think
Neighborhood Watch Commander is probably super-good for weenie
Auspex...)

I'm not quite sure I see how Perfectionist is so fantastic. I know
that there are some decks which feature minions that people don't
normally bother trying to block (Hesha comes to mind), but for the
part I think part this card is only going to be good for
rush/combat-heavy decks, and then only when someone doesn't have
a disposable minion to throw in your way (or just a Wake that they
want to cycle without bothering to do anything). Capitalist, on the
other hand, is probably better, as most minions will bleed at some
point in the game. Capitalist also works well in both stealth/bleed and
bruise/bleed decks, as well being better than hunting for a minion
who's only bleeding for one when there are more dangerous minions on
the table (Isabel Giovanni bleeding for one when Andrea and Gillespi
are still untapped, for instance), whereas Perfectionist seems more
suited to a narrower range of deck types. Of course, I have no
personal play data on Perfectionist yet - anybody want to fill me
in as to how well it works in real play? :)

John Eno
Prince of Pittsburgh

Messages.Author: John Alston
Messages.Body:
Of course, I have no
> personal play data on Perfectionist yet - anybody want to fill me
> in as to how well it works in real play? :)
>

So nicely in Canberra at prerelease that people were suggesting that it is
broken. I think this card will surprise you into realising just how many
actions go without reaction cards being played.

Having said that, I really like Curmudgeon which no-one seems to have
commented on so far. It's a trifle! and again at prerelease, it was
surprising to see the addtional thought of my prey go into acting with a
minion who had been targetted. Cards like this I think work because no-one
sees them as overpowered (not painting a bullseye on your minions is good.)
And did I mention its a trifle?

John

My list of good/bad not already mentioned:

The GOOD:

Approximation of Loyalty. Finally Presence can (kind of) seduce! One
of the effects that were missing considering the discipline´s most
basic uses.. hehe.
Now all we need is Strike: Combat Ends for Obfuscate! :D BTW, did you
know that in the RPG, this power is actually called Approximation fo
Loyalty ABSOLUTE, and requires Presence AND Dominate? Guess they left
out any absoluteness along with the DOM! :D

Descent into Darkness. COOL COOL COOL!! Did I mention COOL? New effect
with lots of potential. So, you Sensory Deprived me? No problem, my
last action will be to leave play until your Ravnos gets diablerized!
Temptation? OK, here´s one vampire you´re NEVER going to steal!
Derange? Ok, so i´m a crazy Malk, with an urge to visit the Abyss!! :D
And they come back ready for another Minion Tap!

Occlusion: Simple. Elegant. VERY Effective.

Petra. Sexiest Nos ever! Move over Lucretia!

Baldesar Rossellini. FANTASTIC! (I wish he were a Setite) He could
even fit in some Lasombra Bruise decks with just a little trouble.
Mausoleum, Morgue and Tower of Lonson for 3pool!!!!

Crocodile´s Tongue. Combine this with Approximation of Loyalty for
some powerfull Toreador decks!

Cavalcade of Great Sabbat Vampires. Almost ALL of them are fantastic!
Marthe, Bruce, Cyseck, Una, Jesse, Hartmut, John Paleologus, Shawnda
and Marie are so good they just scream to be used right away! :)

The BAD:

Revelations of Desire. Should be called: Left A LOT to Desire. Lousy
bleed modifier with conditional superior use. For a clan with
Presence, Night Moves, Spying Mission, Enticement and Edge Vitiation,
this becoems wallpaper quickly. Also does NOT synergize as well as it
might seem with Corruption decks as it forces you to burn a counter,
further increasing the already high mumber of actions such a deck
needs. Cute for the occasinal susprise factor only.

Diamond Thunderbolt. Completely screws Form/Corruption decks. It WILL
see some play as it also hoses Graverobbing (with or without
Baltimore), Mind Rape, Spirit Marrionette and Malkavian Dementia
decks. Hand Jam is not a factor since it can be used to give blood as
well.

Seren Sukardi (or Seren Sucks-Hard as he is already being called
around here). Why bother with a special power that will never see any
use? For added sarcasm, he gets superior Thaumaturgy, so whenever you
think of using it, you also think: Press+Walk of Flame is SO MUCH
easier, why bother yet again? And the Setites remain with only one
7cap with all in-clans at superior and one 8cap with all in-clans at
superior. Also, ZERO new vampires with serpentis in Gehenna other than
the two Setites. So basically, they get frozen till February.
A lot more so than the other indies, who at least share discipline
spreads with other clans.

(yes, I like Setites)

Umm..... not much else really, all the other bummy cards have been
mentioned. Most of the new set is awesome. And I donpt think the
events will destroy play as some people think. The hand-jam and chaos
factors will dissuade most people from using them heavilly after the
initial fad.

Daniel.

worth a masterslot.

Personal Involvment: In what decks can this card be effective?

Poison Pill: There are other reaction vs votes that are better and
still doesn´t see any play.

Traditionalist: Even with trifle, it´s a weak card. How many times
will this happen in a normal game?

/Mathias

If you bounce a bleed to your prey, your Conniver gains a blood. If your
prey takes a point of damage from a cross-table KRC or Malkavian Foo, your
Conniver gains a blood.

blood if the action is blocked, or if *any* reaction cards are played,

silly successful-hunt reaction cards.

Messages.Author: Wes
Messages.Body:
"Gregory Stuart Pettigrew" <ethe...@sidehack.sat.gweep.net> wrote

>
> If you bounce a bleed to your prey, your Conniver gains a blood. If
your
> prey takes a point of damage from a cross-table KRC or Malkavian Foo,
your
> Conniver gains a blood.

(Note that you would have to *successfully* bounce the bleed. If your
prey blocked/reduced etc then you would *not* gain the blood.)

Yes... but so what?

Which do you expect to see more:

1) One of your vampire's actions not being reacted to at all
2) Successfully bouncing a bleed/cross-table love

Probably depends on how your deck is built, but in most decks I would
say #1 is more common than #2. Big time.

I'm not saying Conniver is a bad card. I am saying that it is inferior
in most situations to Perfectionist.

Note also that the two cards, though archetypes, are very different in
scope. It would be better to compare Perfectionist to the more proactive
archetypes such as Capitalist, Bravo, etc. In fact, I would say that is
another reason to prefer Perfectionist, because of its proactiveness.
With Conniver, you are relying on someone else to do something before
you get the blood. Me, I'd rather have control over when I get it.

> > But you could conceivably use Perfectionist on *any* action. A hunt
becomes
> > a hunt for 2. A vote also becomes a hunt. A bleed also becomes a
hunt. A
> > recruit ally action also becomes a hunt.
> >
> > Sure, someone could cycle a wake to make you not gain a blood, but I
see
> > that as an accpetable risk. Hell, let them cycle their wakes! That
means one
> > less blocking minion when I do something nasty to them :)
>
> Or they could just block you and kill you.

Well, duh... yeah. But they could do that anyway, right? What does that
have to do with the relative value of Perfectionist?

> All this Perfectionist-happiness forgets that the minion does not gain
> blood if the action is blocked, or if *any* reaction cards are played,
> including intercept (even if the block fails) or bounce, or even those
> silly successful-hunt reaction cards.

I have not forgotten the conditions of Perfectionist. Each archetype has
conditions. The conditions for Perfectionist are less drastic than those
of the other archetypes. I would add an "IMHO" to that, but I think that
most people would agree with me.

Cheers,
WES

> avoid.

That's true, but again, it's _costing you nothing_ to have that
corner-case ability. You haven't lost out on any discipline or other
special.

When Emmit is saying 'it's free', he doesn't mean 'it costs Seren
nothing' - he means it is costing you the player nothing to have this
ability on Seren.

Yes, it's not likely to come up, and it's not all that easy to build
for. But when you are building your deck, there's no cost to your
crypt for him to have the ability. He's still a 7-cap with 7 levels of
disciplines; the fact that he has a very corner-case special is
entirely and totally a (very small) added bonus that has zero penalty
to your deck, even if you are NOT ever planning to use it. It has
absolutely no downside, because it has no penalty and at worst you
simply don't ever use his special - in which case he's still a
correctly-powered vampire.

> Daniel.

-John Flournoy

Messages.Author: Gregory Stuart Pettigrew
Messages.Body:


Personal Involvement [Gehenna:R]
Cardtype: Master
Cost: 3 pool
Master.
If your prey has more pool than you (after paying the cost of this card),
your prey burns 3 pool. Any Methuselah can cancel this card as it is
played by burning 2 pool (the cost of this card is not paid in that case).

When you play this card, one of three things will happen:

1. You and your prey each burn 3 pool. Not the most amazing master in the
world, but if you can beat him by attrition, it will help.

2. The card is Suddened. Drat.

3. The card is cancelled via its own card text. A good chunk of the time,
this will be by your prey, who cannot afford to lose 3 pool to you (You
bleed machine, you), and must live with 2 pool loss. True, someone else
could cancel it (even you), but it still costs them 2 pool.

Nobody said it was good, but Seren having it doesn't make him bad.
He's a Setite with superior thaumaturgy, who gives a shit if he even
has a special. Someone with SER who can clean the blood off a vamp in
combat sounds pretty good to me. With access to Form of Corruption,
Temptation, Theft of Vitae, Skin of the Adder, Apportation, B2W, Walk
of Flame and The Jones this is far from a fragile slithering snake.
Yet, he still has the ability to S:CE if need be. You use to have to
pay 10 for a vamp who could do this (and she had, lo and behold,a
crappy rarely used special). How often have you read Qufur's special
and wished it wasn't completey useless, is he bad because of it?
Hardly.

And you also state that Revelations of Desire is crap as well, are you
on Opium? (apparently not). Lalitha, Celine, Khalil, and Aabbt Kindred
are all a little scarier now. We know you'll block or deflect if they
open with a pre bleed action (which 2 of them can't do) but now if you
don't block you can get bled for 2 anyway. If you do block you can get
Venenationed and now Nerfertiti can bleed you for +3. If you bounce
her the +3 does not affect any other Methuselah, and you had better be
above 6 or she will Approximation of Loyalty and you will eat that
bleed, now that is Setite reponsible bleed! If you bouce one of the
little ones we can let the new Meth block and Venenate for later use.
We can save our stealth for when we want to pull the Enticement out on
the same turn (Nerfertiti untapping due to self Temptation or with her
new li'l buddy Mylan Horseed). Mylan, Revelations of Desire and
Approximation of Loyalty are just incredibly cool new weapons to add
to the Setite arsenal (not to mention the anarch cards). I can't
believe that you are the one who wrote the latest FoS newsletter.

Robert Scythe, the most prolific user of Serpentis/Setites in L.A. and
Orange Counties (did I mention Nehsi?)
